lesson_title: The Two-Number Game: Factorising Trinomials in Twenty Seconds
hook_text: x squared plus 8x plus 15. Two numbers, two clues, one answer. Here is the game that factorises every Grade 9 trinomial.
clip_script: x squared plus 8x plus 15 came from two brackets: x plus something, x plus something else. Find the two somethings. Clue one: they multiply to the end number, 15. Clue two: they add to the middle number, 8. Pairs that multiply to 15: 1 and 15, 3 and 5. Which adds to 8? 3 and 5. Answer: the bracket x plus 3 times the bracket x plus 5. Multiply it back out: x squared, 5x, 3x, 15. Original. Done. Signs? Last number minus means the two numbers have different signs, so look for a difference instead: x squared minus 3x minus 10 wants 2 and 5 with the bigger one negative. The bracket x plus 2 times the bracket x minus 5. Two clues, one pair, multiply back to check. That is the whole game.
visual_style: A trinomial on a whiteboard with two empty brackets below it; factor pairs appear in a column and all but one are struck through in red; the winning pair slides into the brackets and a multiply-back check ticks green.
pacing: A fast setup, a visible hunt through the pairs, a clean win and a one-line sign rule.
